newsitem.title: USA: Czech Republic's Havel receives, drops award.
newsitem.headline: Czech Republic's Havel receives, drops award.

text.p: Czech Republic President Vaclav Havel on Thursday night accepted and promptly dropped an award from the Institute for EastWest Studies for his deft handling of his country's reconciliation with Germany.
The bridge-like crystal fell to the floor of a Waldorf Astoria ballroom as Havel accepted the award from U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

"For those of us that were born in Czechoslovakia and were proud of having been born there, but kept our heads low from 1948 ... until 1990, Vaclav Havel has made us proud to have been born Czech," Albright said.
German President Roman Herzog also accepted the institute's European Statesman Award.
Havel said Europeans were grateful for American efforts to protect human rights in Europe, but that in the future Europeans will do more of the work.
"We are prepared to stand up (for) ourselves for freedom on our continent and take upon ourselves an increasing share of the joint defence of our shared values," Havel said.

After the ceremony the institute surprised Albright, who was celebrating her 60th birthday on Thursday, with her favourite flowers -- salmon-coloured roses -- and her favourite dessert -- chocolate cake.
The ballroom then filled with hundreds of dignitaries and guests rose to sing "Happy Birthday, Madame Secretary."
"If you've got to be 60, this is the way to do it," Albright said.
